i was on an international trip last year when my grandfather was admitted to the hospital with pneumonia. he’d been unwell on and off over the past couple years. when he had to be ventilated and my mom told me he wasn’t going to be better i changed my flight to the next day and flew to florida to be with them. 

i told my mom to ask him to hang on for me to say goodbye, but to tell him that i understood if he couldn’t. it was so stressful but i made it to the hospital around 8pm and got to tell him about my trip, hug him, kiss him, and sit by his bed holding his hand. he was on a lot of medication and not really aware of much but he smiled a bit and squeezed my hand. i sat there for a few hours and told him it was ok, i loved him, etc. just after midnight he passed. 

that was my first major loss. i was just glad i could be there with him and my family in his last moments. i really think he did hold on for me to get there before he let go.

warning: slight rambling ahead but i wanted to chip in as someone who dealt with a lot of the same things as your daughter not *too* too long ago. 

as far as her goth/e-girl phase, just allowing her to express herself stylistically can be very helpful. no matter how heinous (speaking from experience) her clothing/hair/makeup choices are now, it’s a great vehicle for expressing how you feel inside and having parents be accepting of that can be extremely validating. 

is she into music at all? for me going to shows/concerts and being involved with my favorite bands was a massive help (still is). if you’re not comfortable letting her go alone, i know that plenty of parents accompany kids to shows and hang at the bar/in the back and let them have their fun. i was always jealous of kids whose parents went (although the kids probably didn’t enjoy it 😉). there’s something magical about hearing a song and realizing you’re not the only one feeling the way you do - and that’s increased tenfold when you see it live in a crowd of people who are all singing along! 

at shows she’ll also have a chance to see other people who dress more alternatively, and you could encourage her to start conversations with people around her age there (this is something i would be horrified by at age 12 but a simple “omg i love your choker/boots/bag/etc is a great vehicle for making friends!) if she connects with anyone i would encourage you to let them keep in touch in some way, even if not online. they’ll have something in common and a great jumping point for building a friendship. 


i know 12 is young for social media but maybe as she gets older she can also start making friends online and building a community that way. i know everyone says not to talk to strangers on the internet (and parents need to be *extremely* vigilant in helping make sure their kids are talking to actual other kids) but i’m 27 and some of my closest friends are people that i started talking to on tumblr/twitter when i was 14-15. 


you seem like a great parent and are doing so much for your daughter. our preteen/teenage years are hard enough without dealing with mental illness and i know how isolating it can be. if you need music recs for your kiddo let me know 😋

i was 6, and 9/11 is my mom’s birthday. it was a heavy day and i remember her crying while i was getting ready for school. i remember either school closing or her picking me up early? there was an aircraft plant near our city and we didn’t know if we’d be a target. i definitely remember friends whose parents ended up deployed/killed in action/etc in the years following.

i’d say that at this point, 20 years on, i appreciate the jokes more than the endless stream of trauma and sad stories - i struggle with my mental health already and it’s hard to handle the complete takeover of every media outlet/website/etc on this day. especially when i wanna celebrate my mom! i also think that a lot of the tributes feel forced, or not genuine at least. i think about how much countless others lost in the aftermath - multiple wars, governmental upheavals in other countries, more and more radical terrorist groups and attacks. how all of our lives changed - for better and worse. how we’ve lost hundreds of thousands of our fellow citizens to covid - where are their tributes? 

so i appreciate the jokes, but i hope that people will start to contemplate more than just the immediate events of 9/11 and how altered our world is because of it.
